item.title: Controlling Gradle's Java Compiler Version: Multiple Configuration Methods
item.description:
“Controlling Gradle’s Java Compiler Version: Multiple Configuration Methods”

When working with Java projects managed by Gradle, precisely controlling which Java Development Kit (JDK) is used for compiling source code is crucial for maintaining compatibility and adhering to project specifications. The mechanisms for achieving this are varied, depending on your Gradle version, operating system, and preferred configuration scope (global vs. project-specific).

How can developers reliably specify the Java compiler executable or the home directory for the JDK that Gradle utilizes during a build process?

item.title: Fixing React Native Android Build Failures Post 0.71.0-rc0 Release
item.description:
“Fixing React Native Android Build Failures Post 0.71.0-rc0 Release”

Facing unexpected Android build failures in a React Native project, especially if the issue arose without recent code modifications? A known cause centers around the publication of React Native version 0.71.0-rc0. This situation often manifests as dependency resolution problems where Gradle fetches an incorrect or incompatible version of the React Native Android library from public repositories like Maven Central instead of the local one bundled with the npm package.

item.title: Gradle: Add Local JAR Dependencies Effectively
item.description:
“Gradle: Add Local JAR Dependencies Effectively”

When developing projects, especially in environments like Android or other Java-based applications managed by Gradle, you might encounter situations where you need to include local JAR files as dependencies. These libraries might not be available in public repositories like Maven Central, or they might be proprietary. Gradle provides several flexible ways to manage these local JAR dependencies. This discussion explores various accepted solutions for incorporating local JAR files into your Gradle build.
